what_it_does: Training a large neural network across many machines requires each machine to compute gradients (signals indicating how much each weight should change) and then share those gradients with every other machine so all machines stay in sync — a step called all-reduce (a collective communication operation where every participant contributes and receives a combined result). Sending every gradient over the network is expensive and often the main bottleneck. PacTrain attacks this from two angles: it actively prunes (removes) unimportant weights from the network during training, which makes most gradients exactly zero and therefore not worth sending; and it uses knowledge of where those zeros are to compress the remaining gradients more aggressively before transmission. Because the sparsity pattern is known in advance, the compression is lightweight and does not add significant computation overhead.
